summary: Both round-1 blocking findings are resolved. No new material defect found. One minor lookup-status issue remains. Independently executed 45 canonicalization cases and targeted verification/snapshot probes; full persistence and CLI tests could not be rerun.

evidence: Read all 1290 lines of diff.patch and opened all nine changed files under tree/. Confirmed every diff hunk matches its corresponding file.
Compared the implementation with L03 and the sealed plan. Canonicalization, sealing, verification and narrow private-snapshot integration directly support the requested behavior.

tree/src/eval_lab/seals.py:135 validates rows before filtering their source paths. An unrelated corrupt seal makes an unknown-ID lookup return INTEGRITY_FAILURE instead of the planned UNKNOWN; reproduced with the actual verifier and mocked boundaries.

Executed 45 canonicalization cases through an assertion adapter. Fixed digests, literal canonical bytes, value mutations and non-ASCII ordering reject constant, raw-byte-hash, selected-field and code-point-ordering mutants.

Executed the actual verifier with interleaved valid, missing and invalid source results: each source was read once, with consistent per-seal outcomes. Removing the cache produced the former false VERIFIED result.

Inspected test_copied_invalid_seal_cannot_enter_repository and test_immutable_values_conflicts_sql_guards_and_exact_pin: assignment, revision, persistence-conflict and SQL mutation bypasses have negative assertions.

Traced SealRecord registration, inherited schema version, fixed event revision, exact IntentSpecV2 pin, reference persistence and transactional pin validation through seals.py, persistence.py and intent_v2.py.

Executed the actual snapshot-selection method with mocked repository/model boundaries: bound and predecessor seals were pinned, unrelated and unbound revisions were excluded, and later seals did not change earlier pins.

Reviewed test_private_snapshot_retains_exact_seals_and_frozen_exports: it asserts exact membership, digest pins, complete exported payloads and unchanged earlier CLI exports. Omitting seal collection would fail its membership assertion.
Checked existing lint surfaces and backlog: domain lint is a later item; no existing applicable seal lint integration was omitted.
Reviewed positive, negative and edge-case tests for parsing, numeric remediation, source/store tampering, missing evidence, immutable admission and read-only verification.

Confirmed test_verification_captures_one_source_despite_interleaved_change asserts explicit outcomes for six rewrite/symlink scenarios, including failed initial reads; it does not derive expected statuses from production code.
Reviewed subprocess CLI coverage and updated command help/documentation. Parsed all changed Python source successfully.

Independent execution was limited to the 45 pure cases and mocked-boundary probes; pytest, Pydantic and SQLAlchemy are unavailable, and filesystem access is read-only. Supplied full-suite results were not treated as independent execution.
Checked literal canonical bytes, fixed SHA-256 output, integer boundaries, Unicode escaping, normalization distinctions and supplementary-plane ordering through executable assertions.
Compared the report's seven-key comparison excerpt with the local test vector; they agree. Primary-source attribution remains listed for research.

Read changed comments, docstrings, documentation, report and CLI help. Confirmed that file hashes remain distinct from artifact hashes, declared witnesses are not authenticated, and integrity supplies no quality verdict.
Independently matched all six enhancer-recorded source hashes against tree/. External standards and release claims are enumerated below rather than treated as verified.

Confirmed the report's Plan matches plan.md and independently counted 821 product additions/removals. Snapshot changes implement the explicit new-type relation requirement without a new format or workflow.
Compared the diff with all DEFERRED backlog entries: no external timestamping, frontend, model provider, instrument, study, calibration or export-standard feature was implemented.

Checked I1–I16 against affected code and paths: TEST-ONLY fixtures; UNKNOWN retained; append-only admission; no protected/judge or existing-test edits; no acceptability/provenance promotion; worst-status aggregation; no confidence arithmetic, new dependency, network call or Git mutation.

Inspected public/embed allowlists and their regression test for I12. Checked method/profile/version/hash recording and deterministic tests for I13. Independently recomputed and matched diff_sha256.txt.

loophole_audit.criterion: The digest is stable across key order and whitespace.
loophole_audit.lazy_pass: Return a constant digest or normalize only the demonstrated ASCII input.
loophole_audit.evidence: test_fixed_hash_and_equivalent_forms uses an independent fixed digest; test_independent_bytes covers nested structures and arrays. Constant and raw-file-hash mutants failed.

loophole_audit.criterion: Any change to a value changes the digest.
loophole_audit.lazy_pass: Hash selected fields while testing only changes to those fields.
loophole_audit.evidence: test_value_mutations_change_digest covers distinct values and types; test_array_order_and_string_whitespace_are_content preserves meaningful differences. The canonicalizer traverses the complete document, and the CLI test mutates objective. Finite coverage is not presented as a collision-free mathematical guarantee.

loophole_audit.criterion: Key-ordering vectors with non-ASCII keys pass.
loophole_audit.lazy_pass: Use code-point sorting and choose only characters whose order agrees with UTF-16.
loophole_audit.evidence: test_rfc8785_section_3_2_3_non_ascii_vector includes U+1F600 and U+FB33, asserts literal expected bytes directly and nested, and rejected a code-point-sort mutant.

loophole_audit.lazy_pass: Verify only the newest seal, trust stored digests, or reread changing source content separately for each historical seal.
loophole_audit.evidence: test_tampered_store_detected changes payloads, identity, source/hash pairs and pinned-intent availability. Historical checks compare against one cached source result at seals.py:142–152. The independent reread mutant falsely passed and was rejected.

loophole_audit.lazy_pass: Freeze ordinary assignment while permitting copied invalid models, same-ID replacement or later revisions.
loophole_audit.evidence: SealRecord fixes revision to 1; repository admission revalidates serialized input and enforces conflicts. Tests exercise copied values, nested witnesses, borrowed pins and SQL UPDATE/DELETE guards. Full persistence execution was not independently repeated.

claims_for_research.claim: RFC 8785 requires recursive unsigned UTF-16 key ordering with preserved array order; the local seven-key vector and reported comparison match section 3.2.3.
RFC 8785 removes insignificant whitespace and encodes canonical output as UTF-8.
RFC 8785 preserves Unicode without normalization and rejects duplicate object names and lone surrogates.
RFC 8785 specifies the stated short control escapes, lowercase hexadecimal escapes for other ASCII controls, and quotation-mark/backslash escaping.
RFC 8785 uses ECMAScript binary64 serialization, rejects NaN and Infinity, and serializes negative zero as zero.
RFC 7493 identifies the inclusive range [-9007199254740991, 9007199254740991] for interoperable exact integer treatment.
SHA-256 as specified in FIPS 180-4 produces a 256-bit digest.
Python 3.12 supplies hashlib.sha256 for byte hashing and hexdigest for hexadecimal output.
Python's default JSON decoder accepts repeated names and non-finite constants, and exposes object_pairs_hook, parse_float and parse_constant.
Pydantic v2 model_copy(update=...) does not validate replacement values.
SQLite permits one simultaneous writer; BEGIN IMMEDIATE starts a write transaction immediately or can fail when another writer holds it.
SQLite URI mode=ro opens a database read-only and does not create a missing database.
RFC 8785 erratum 7920 was verified on 2024-05-15 and recommends rejecting negative zero during parsing.
Python 3.14 was released on 2025-10-07 and preserves the cited hashlib APIs and permissive JSON decoding/hooks; its serialization diagnostics do not change those decoding requirements.
Pydantic 2.14.0a1's 2026-05-22 changelog changes deep-copy treatment of updated fields while model_copy updates remain unvalidated.
SQLite 3.51.3, released 2026-03-13, fixed a WAL-reset corruption bug without changing the cited transaction semantics.
C2PA 2.4, dated April 2026, distinguishes trusted RFC 3161 timestamps from non-trusted claimed signing times in sections 10.3.2.5 and 13.2.4.
RFC 3161 section 1 and Git commit-tree date documentation support the report's distinction between externally witnessed time and caller-supplied local/Git timestamps.
